roleTitle: Capacity Planning Analyst, Wealth Services Platform
jobDescription: The wealth services platform of a private bank processes portfolio valuations, client statements and adviser reports on a monthly cycle. The Capacity Planning Analyst forecasts batch-processing demand for the month-end cycle, plans compute and storage capacity with the platform team, and is expected to keep month-end batch overruns down, with results reported against the platform's published overrun baseline.
requirements: Forecasts month-end batch demand from client, account and report volumes and maintains the demand model.
Plans compute and storage capacity for the month-end cycle with the platform team.
Reduces month-end batch overruns, reported against the published overrun baseline.
Coordinates capacity changes with the platform and finance teams and records own responsibility boundaries.
Documents model assumptions, known limitations and hand-over conditions for each planning cycle.

evidence.text: Maintained the month-end demand model that forecasts batch volume from client, account and report counts, refreshing the coefficients each quarter from the platform's job-history tables.
Planned compute and storage for each month-end cycle with the platform team, translating the forecast into node reservations and storage headroom in the capacity plan.

Month-end batch overruns fell from 9 per cycle to 2 per cycle over the six cycles after the re-sequenced valuation jobs went live, as recorded in the platform's overrun report against its published baseline of 9 overruns per cycle for the preceding half-year.

Coordinated capacity changes with the platform and finance teams in the monthly capacity review; reservation changes were approved by the platform manager and the cost impact was signed off by finance.

Wrote the assumptions note for each planning cycle, listing the model coefficients, the known limitation that ad-hoc adviser reports were outside the forecast and the hand-over items for the next cycle.

Work sample: the overrun report extract for the six cycles (overruns per cycle, baseline line, go-live marker for the re-sequenced jobs) and the assumptions note for one cycle, with the report's export identifiers as a verification trail.

Reference call with former platform manager: confirmed the overrun figures come from the platform's monthly overrun report, that the re-sequencing of valuation jobs was the candidate's proposal, and the employment dates.
Recruiter logistics note: candidate can start after a four-week notice period and is available for a follow-up call next week.
